title: Send each colour to its belt in Ladder
summary: Read the colour of each workpiece that waits at the stop blade, push the red ones onto the side belt and let the blue ones ride on.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show sensor response time or belt speed.
objectives: Decide a route from one sensor result once the part lies still.
Run a push as a short sequence: extend until Extended, retract until Retracted.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/ColourSeparation.ld.json, run the three belts after Start and hold each workpiece at the blade. Wait for it to lie still, then read IsRed: push a red one onto the side belt, release a blue one.
stages.checkpoint: Red workpieces end in RedBin, blue ones in BlueBin, and Done lights after the eighth.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, decide what the blade and the pusher do for each colour. A red workpiece stays held while the plate pushes it out; a blue one is released. When may the blade hold again?
stages.checkpoint: A red workpiece stays held while the plate works; a blue one needs the blade down. When the blade may rise again is the decision of the practice.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter has no rungs, so no belt moves and no workpiece is sorted; run the belts after Start, read IsRed once the workpiece is still, push red ones out and release blue ones.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named colour-separation and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}: a red workpiece stops at the blade, the plate pushes it onto the side belt and the next one waits; a blue one passes straight on to the outfeed.
stages.checkpoint: Push never goes TRUE for a blue workpiece.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The EVENTUALLY assertion proves both bins received a workpiece; the ALWAYS assertion proves none went to the wrong bin and none was dropped; the AT assertions pin the lamps.
stages.checkpoint: The grade sees the bins, not the colour your program read.

hints.text: Think about what the program has to remember from one scan to the next, and which input tells you that each movement of the plate has finished.

Keep the step in a state number: 0 wait for a still workpiece, 1 push, 2 retract, 3 let a blue one go. A TON of T#300ms on Waiting gives the settle time. Leave state 0 with two rungs: a normally open contact of IsRed goes to state 1, a normally closed one to state 3. A pushed workpiece is handled when Retracted is TRUE; a released one is handled when it has left the blade (for example a TON of T#1500ms on NOT Waiting; the time is a choice, not a requirement). Drive Hold from Active in series with an NE block on State and 3, and count with a CTU of 8.

faultCases: The starter has no rungs, so no belt moves and no workpiece is sorted; run the belts after Start, read IsRed once the workpiece is still, push red ones out and release blue ones.
